Description: A large gypsum relief from Courtyard VIII of the palace of Sargon II at Dur-Sharrukin (Khorsabad), extending over three complete slabs and at least a fourth incomplete slab, now in the Louvre. It depicts a great convoy of boats on stylized waves - teeming with fish, crabs, tortoises, and sea creatures - carrying or towing hewn cedar timbers, with other boats returning empty for a new load. The two fortresses in the scene have been read as Tyre and Arwad, or as Cyprus and a Phoenician port.
Interpretations: The relief documents the Lebanon timber trade that supplied both Assyrian palaces and, a century earlier, Solomon's temple - the same cedar, the same Phoenician shippers, the same coast. The identification of the fortresses is debated, so the scene should be described as a timber convoy, not firmly as a Tyre tribute scene. It illuminates the logistics behind 1 Kings 5 and Ezra 3:7, where cedar from Lebanon is floated down for the temple.
BiblicalSignificance: It shows how Lebanon cedar actually reached Mesopotamia - by Phoenician ship - the supply chain behind the temple-building accounts of Kings and Ezra.
DiscoveryLocation: Khorsabad, Iraq (Dur-Sharrukin, palace of Sargon II)
